title: The Trick a 9-Year-Old Used to Add 1 to 100 in Seconds
description: The staircase trick young Carl Friedrich Gauss used to instantly sum 1+2+3+...+100 -- and the general formula it reveals: n(n+1)/2.
narration_lines: One plus two plus three, all the way up to one hundred. As the story goes, a nine year old named Gauss solved this in seconds. Here's how.
Line the numbers up as a staircase of blocks, one for each number from one to one hundred.
Now flip a copy upside down, and slide it in to pair each number with its opposite.
Every single pair adds up to exactly one hundred and one. One plus a hundred. Two plus ninety nine. Three plus ninety eight. And so on, all the way down.
That's one hundred pairs, of one hundred and one each. And since we doubled everything to make the pairs, we just cut the total in half.
One hundred, times one hundred and one, divided by two, equals... five thousand and fifty.
